title: Verdant Systems POC: Eval scope, golden prompts & hallucination plan
summary: Intro POC scoping for Verdant. Agreed success metrics (precision/recall style scoring for extraction tasks, <5% critical hallucination rate), baseline workload shape and target RPS, golden prompt set and regression test cadence. Discussed security constraints (VPC, audit logs) and timeline to prototype in 6 weeks.
topics: Workload sizing and synthetic load shape
Golden prompts and regression test set
Benchmarks: latency, throughput, cost per 1k tokens
action_items: Maya: Send tailored POC statement of work and pricing ranges by 2026-12-03
Liam: Share benchmark template and suggested load generator config (k6 + sample queries) by 2026-12-06
Eleanor: Provide 300 anonymized production examples and 50 failure cases by 2026-12-07
Marco: Confirm network constraints and whether VPC peering or Private deployment needed by 2026-12-04
next_steps: Review SOW and accept provisional scope
Kickoff internal infra prep once SOW signed
Schedule 1-hr technical runbook review (SE + Verdant infra) next week
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-30 16:00 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes | Attendees: Maya, Liam (Redwood); Eleanor, Marco, Sofia (Verdant)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — align on success criteria for the POC, agree on workload and benchmarks, and nail down the golden prompt set and hallucination checks. Is that good for folks?
[00:10] Eleanor (Verdant): Yep, that works. Quick note — our timeline is a bit aggressive, leadership wants a demo in about 6 weeks so we need to be pragmatic.
[00:20] Marco (Verdant): Also FYI we have network restrictions, V P C peering is possible but on-prem air gap is not an option for the first phase.
[00:30] Liam (Redwood SE): Understood. For performance we'll scope hosted Dedicated or Redwood Dedicated — sorry, Redwood Dedicaed — and can show a Hosted baseline first.
[00:40] Sofia (Verdant): On success criteria, we care about two things: extraction accuracy from clinical notes and hallucination rate on entity outputs. For the former we want F1 > 0.88 on named entities in the golden set, and for hallucination less than 5% on critical fields.
[01:02] Maya: That seems reasonable. Do you have a preferred scoring approach? Micro-F1 for extraction and a separate binary hallucination label?
[01:10] Eleanor: Yes, micro-F1 plus a manual review on a 10% sample to validate. For hallucination we want an automated heuristic plus human confirmation for any flagged items.
[01:22] Liam: For the automated detection we usually run a set of format checks (schema validation), then a prompt-based sanity check to detect unsupported claims. Example: if the model invents a medication that doesn't appear in the record, it's flagged. We can surface that as a boolean and an explanation blob — excuse me, explanation text — for triage.
[01:45] Marco: How noisy is the detection? We can't have too many false positives since SOC and our triage team are small.
[01:50] Liam: We'll tune thresholds. Initial run will aim for high recall (catch most hallucinations) and then tune to lower FP once we have labeled data.
[02:04] Sofia: About workload sizing — our production writes about 2,000 requests/day for the ingestion pipeline, but for the POC we want to test up to 50 RPS sustained for short burst tests. We also have a long tail of 60-90 token prompts and some 800-token context threads.
[02:25] Maya: Good, so test mix: 70% short prompts (~60 tokens), 20% mid (~300 tokens), 10% long (~800 tokens). We'll create a synthetic load profile to mirror that.
[02:40] Eleanor: We also have stateful chat flows where KV cache usage matters — sometimes users call back older context. Ensure the eval includes cold and warm cache runs.
[02:53] Liam: We'll include cold/warm KV cache scenarios. Note — transcription: you might see 'K V cash' in logs, sorry auto-transcribe quirk.
[03:05] Marco: Security — we need SSO, SAML, RBAC, and audit logs. Any encryption key integrations? We would prefer KMS/H S M style key control.
[03:18] Maya: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit log exports. For the POC, we can do a limited access Hosted+VPC with audit streaming to your logging bucket. We'll attach the security docs after the call.
[03:30] Sofia: Perfect. Back to benchmarks: what's the acceptance on latency? We want median latency under 350ms for short prompts at 50 RPS if possible.
[03:44] Liam: For short prompts that's achievable on Dedicated with batching tuned for low-latency. We'll run baseline profiling — average and p95 — and include cost-per-1k tokens estimates.
[03:58] Eleanor: For golden prompts, we can provide canonical cases — about 150 examples covering typical entities and edge cases. We'll mark maybe 20 as 'must-pass' critical cases.
[04:12] Maya: Great. Our approach: you provide golden set + negative/failure examples. Redwood will build the regression suite and run nightly regressions during the POC window. We'll report a quality score composed of weighted F1 (60%), hallucination rate penalty (30%), format compliance (10%).
[04:34] Sofia: Can you unpack format compliance?
[04:37] Liam: Sure. Format compliance checks that the model output matches the schema: required fields present, enumerated values within allowed set, date formats parse. Non-compliance is a hard fail for certain fields — like 'dosage' — and counts as a reduction in the quality score.
[04:54] Marco: How will we handle human-in-the-loop review for borderline cases? We have limited reviewers.
[04:59] Maya: We'll provide sampling rules: we flag any output with hallucination score above threshold or format checks failed and then sample at 10% for review. We can automate triage to minimize reviewer load.
[05:12] Eleanor: Timelines — if we finalize SOW this week, can Redwood start infra and load testing in two weeks?
[05:20] Maya: Yes, that's feasible. SOW accepted -> infra prep -> data ingestion and golden prompt handoff -> week of profiling and baseline run -> then iterative tuning. 6-week demo target is realistic.
[05:33] Liam: On benchmarking, we'll produce a spreadsheet with columns: prompt_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_ms_median, latency_ms_p95, f1, hallucinated_boolean, format_ok. We'll share that template.
[05:50] Sofia: Please include cost modeling per 1k tokens by model variant in that sheet.
[05:55] Liam: Will do.
[06:00] Maya: Any blocker items?
[06:03] Marco: We need network confirmation and an internal security review slot — I'll book that and share the invite.
[06:09] Eleanor: Also need clarity on data retention during POC — can logs be auto-purged after 30 days?
[06:16] Maya: Yes, we can set retention policy for the POC logs to 30 days and provide export before deletion. We'll include that in the SOW.
[06:25] Sofia: Ok let's recap next steps — SOW, golden set, infra details, benchmark template, and schedule the technical runbook review.
[06:35] Maya: I'll send SOW and security docs by Friday. Liam will send the benchmark template and the load generator config. Marco will confirm VPC detail and retention. Eleanor will share golden set and failure examples.
[06:47] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email; aiming to lock dates this week.
[06:52] Meeting ends.
